scenario.title: Capabilities, settings and secrets
situations: A feature refuses because its project capability is absent.
An operator needs to change one setting or add a credential.
A dashboard inventory appears configured but the underlying service is not ready.
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Which capability refusals already point to their exact setup guide and which only name a capability type?
How are credential materialization and credential readiness verified for each capability outside Onboard?

lessons.title: Inventory is not setup or verification
lessons.when: Choosing a capability or investigating a capability refusal
lessons.need: Read the live project capability roster, then its typed settings and feature-specific setup/probe. The Capabilities page is a readiness inventory, not a setup wizard.
lessons.surface: Docs sidebar -> Capabilities -> capability-settings help; project capability roster.

lessons.title: Choose non-secret settings or secret storage
lessons.when: Before adding or changing provider configuration
lessons.need: Non-sensitive capability settings are a JSON document; secrets use the capability-owned secret surface. Read before CAS replacement; use merge for one path; never print secret values.
lessons.surface: Capabilities guide -> setting help; mistaken scalar settings flags return the correct merge/read/secret recipes.
recipes: yoke projects capability-settings get --project P --cap-type TYPE

lessons.title: Find the right configuration owner
lessons.when: A value could belong to a Pack, project, environment, machine or universe
lessons.need: Separate install-time Pack specialization, live project capability settings, environment settings, machine connections and universe settings. Use the owning registered read/help, not raw config inspection.
lessons.surface: Projects and Capabilities guides explain parts; CLI and config covers the machine/universe boundary.
lessons.gap: No complete scenario-to-owner path was traced for arbitrary feature settings. Do not claim a generic settings UI or validator exists for every capability.
